author: derick-rufino
body:
## [notifications-api] Sistema completo de notificações push (Expo) + alertas de saída iminente

### Contexto

Esta branch implementa a camada de notificações push do sistema de caronas, cobrindo
desde o registro de dispositivos até a entrega de alertas em background (FCM/APNs via
Expo). Inclui também correções de bugs de entrega de notificação identificados durante
o desenvolvimento, cobertura de testes para os novos fluxos e seed de banco realista.

Incorpora os commits da main do Guilherme (viewer OCR/contrato para Admin/Dev +
handler MulterError), resolvidos sem conflito de lógica.

---

### O que foi implementado (derick-rufino)

#### Push Notifications — infraestrutura base
- **`pushService.js`** — encapsula o Expo Server SDK: envio em lote, chunking de 100
  tokens, e enfileiramento de receipt IDs para verificação posterior
- **`notificar.js`** — utilitário centralizado que combina entrega in-app (Socket.io)
  com push de SO (FCM/APNs via Expo). Respeita `per_push_notif` (toggle global) e
  `per_notif_tipos` (por tipo de evento) no servidor, sem lógica duplicada no app
- **`verificarReceiptsPush.js`** — job que consulta a Expo Receipts API e registra
  falhas de entrega permanentes (DeviceNotRegistered → remoção automática do token)
- **Tabela `PUSH_TOKENS`** — 1 device = 1 conta ativa; UPSERT por token; N tokens
  por usuário. Migration em `infosdatabase/create.sql` (v27)
- **Endpoints de token:** `POST /api/usuarios/me/push-token` e
  `DELETE /api/usuarios/me/push-token` via `UsuarioController`
- **`.env.example`** atualizado com `EXPO_ACCESS_TOKEN` (opcional, autentica na Expo)

#### Job: alerta de saída iminente de carona [v28]
- **`alertarCaronaProxima.js`** — node-cron a cada 15 min (fuso BRT): avisa motorista
  e passageiros confirmados sobre caronas que partem nos próximos 15–45 minutos via
  tipo `CARONA_PROXIMA_SAIDA`, canal Android de alta prioridade `caronas`
- Flag `car_alerta_saida_enviado TINYINT(1) DEFAULT 0` em CARONAS garante exatamente
  um alerta por carona entre execuções do cron
- ENUM de NOTIFICACOES estendido com o novo tipo; toggle mapeado a `alteracoes_carona`

#### Correções de bugs de entrega (fix commits)
- **B2 (`SolicitacaoController.responderSolicitacao`):** ao aceitar um passageiro,
  cancela silenciosamente suas outras solicitações pendentes em outras caronas ativas
  e emite `SOLICITACAO_CANCELADA` via socket para cada motorista afetado. Retorna 409
  específico quando motorista tenta aceitar solicitação já auto-cancelada
- **B5 (`CaronaController.deletar`):** captura passageiros com solicitação pendente
  antes do cancelamento e envia `CARONA_CANCELADA` após commit
- **`mensagensSocket`:** sala pessoal `user_<id>` ao conectar; emite
  `mensagem_recebida` para destinatário fora do chat via `.except(sala)`;
  push `MENSAGEM_NOVA` quando destinatário está offline
- **`MensagemController.inbox`:** LEFT JOIN para `outro_id/outro_nome/outro_foto`
  (outro participante da conversa) — frontend não precisa mais chamar endpoint extra
- **`autoCloseCaronas`:** extrai `executarAutoClose()` exportável; motorista recebe
  `CARONA_FINALIZADA` (era `SISTEMA`) para disparar `loadActiveRide` automaticamente
- **`devRoutes`:** `POST /api/dev/jobs/auto-close-caronas` para disparo manual do job
- **`alertarCaronaProxima`:** query de passageiros agora usa UNION com
  `SOLICITACOES_CARONA (sol_status=2)` — corrige passageiros do fluxo de solicitação
  que não recebiam alerta de saída

#### Banco de dados — seed realista (Tupã/SP)
- `insert.sql`: 3 escolas reais (UNESP Tupã, ETEC Massuyuki Kawano), 6 cursos,
  22 usuários cobrindo todo espectro de `usu_verificacao`, 15 caronas (hoje + 4 dias
  futuros + 4 passados), push tokens, penalidades, sugestões e denúncias
- `apagar-banco.sql`: adiciona DROP de PUSH_TOKENS (faltava)
- `delete.sql`: alinhado ao schema atual com Bloco 3 de remoção do seed Tupã

#### Testes
- **4 novas suites** (~700 linhas): `alertar_carona_proxima`, `carona_cancelamento_pendentes`,
  `solicitacao_auto_cancelamento`, `config_preferencias`
- **Mock `expo-server-sdk`** (ESM puro → stub CJS) — isola envio de push em todos os
  testes sem quebrar o Jest
- **`jest.config.js`** atualizado com `moduleNameMapper` para o mock do Expo
- **`NOTAS_TESTES.md`** documentando limitações e observações dos testes

---

### O que veio da main (Guilherme — integrado via merge)

- **Viewer de contrato:** `GET /api/admin/escolas/:esc_id/contrato/arquivo`
  (Dev: qualquer escola; Admin: apenas a própria)
- **Viewer OCR base:** `GET /api/admin/escolas/:esc_id/ocr-base/arquivo`
  (Dev: qualquer escola; Admin: apenas a própria)
- **`MulterError` handler** em `server.js` — erros de upload retornam 400 com mensagem
  legível em vez de 500 (arquivo grande → 10 MB; campo errado; tipo inválido)

Conflito em `documentacao.md` resolvido: bloco Expo Push mantido, versão bumped para
**1.15.0** (reflete features de ambos os lados).

---

### Schema — migrações necessárias

```sql
-- v27: tabela de push tokens
ALTER TABLE CARONAS ADD COLUMN car_alerta_saida_enviado TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

-- v28: flag anti-duplicata de alerta de saída
ALTER TABLE NOTIFICACOES MODIFY COLUMN not_tipo ENUM(
  'CARONA_ACEITA','CARONA_RECUSADA','CARONA_CANCELADA','SOLICITACAO_CANCELADA',
  'NOVA_SOLICITACAO','MENSAGEM_NOVA','CARONA_FINALIZADA',
  'SISTEMA','CARONA_PROXIMA_SAIDA'
) NOT NULL;
-- (script completo em infosdatabase/create.sql)

**Draft, stacked on #422.** Base is `mike/jeev-zero-trust-merge-main` so the diff shows only this trim, not the underlying merge.

Coordinated cloud-side PR will land alongside — appsets reference `crds/flyte-v1/` (going away) and `crds/knative-operator/` (shrinking from 14 to 2 CRDs).

## Why

After the #386 merge, the repo had:

- 12 Knative serving CRDs duplicated between `charts/dataplane/crds/` and `charts/knative-operator/crds/` (and their SSA mirrors at `crds/dataplane/` and `crds/knative-operator/`). Helm warns + skips on default install; otherwise harmless but noisy.
- A separate `crds/flyte-v1/` dir whose single CRD was just a mirror of one file in `charts/dataplane/crds/`. Asymmetric with the `crds/dataplane/` mirror, which already covers the chart dir.

## What

| Path                            | Before                       | After                                             |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `charts/dataplane/crds/`        | 12 knative serving + 1 flyte | unchanged                                         |
| `charts/knative-operator/crds/` | 12 serving + 2 operator      | **2 operator only**                               |
| `crds/dataplane/`               | 12 serving                   | **12 serving + 1 flyte** (mirrors full chart dir) |
| `crds/knative-operator/`        | 12 serving + 2 operator      | **2 operator only**                               |
| `crds/flyte-v1/`                | 1 flyte + scripts/README     | **removed**                                       |

Sync scripts updated to match:

- `crds/dataplane/scripts/sync.sh` now mirrors every `crd-*.yaml` from the chart dir (knative serving + flyte), not just the knative-pattern subset.
- `crds/knative-operator/scripts/sync.sh` filters `operator.yaml` to `.spec.group == "operator.knative.dev"` so only the 2 operator CRDs land.

## Render verification (both modes, with `--include-crds`)

| Mode                                                                     | CRDs rendered                                                    | Duplicates |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| Legacy (`knative-operator.enabled=true`, default)                        | 15 (12 serving + 1 flyte from parent + 2 operator from subchart) | 0          |
| Zero-trust (`zero_trust.enabled=true`, `knative-operator.enabled=false`) | 13 (12 serving + 1 flyte from parent)                            | 0          |

Previously legacy mode emitted 12 "skipping CRD that already exists" warnings; gone.

## Future cleanup breadcrumb

`charts/knative-operator/Chart.yaml` now carries a comment: when zero-trust becomes the only supported mode, delete the subchart + `crds/knative-operator/` + `charts/knative-operator/crds/` together — the 2 operator-type CRDs have no consumer outside the subchart.

## Coordinated cloud PR

Cloud appsets `appset-selfmanaged-dataplane-crds.yaml` and `appset-selfmanaged-data-plane-crds-legacy.yaml` reference both `crds/flyte-v1/` and `crds/knative-operator/`. After this PR lands, those references must change to:

- `crds/dataplane/` (replaces `crds/flyte-v1/` + the serving subset of `crds/knative-operator/`)
- `crds/knative-operator/` kept for the 2 operator CRDs

I'll open the cloud PR next.

make check-vendored-crds  # clean
make helm-test            # clean
make kubeconform-test     # clean
helm template charts/dataplane --include-crds | yq 'select(.kind == "CRD") | .metadata.name' | sort -u  # 15
helm template charts/dataplane --set zero_trust.enabled=true --set knative-operator.enabled=false --include-crds | yq 'select(.kind == "CRD") | .metadata.name' | sort -u  # 13
```

## 요약

`prisma/schema.prisma` 의 `LlmProviderConfig.apiKey` 결정 주석이 **main reality 와 정반대**로 stale 했다. 기존 주석은 "apiKey 는 평문 String — encryption-at-rest 는 ADR-0006 follow-up 책임 … apiKey 컬럼은 평문 저장 placeholder" 라 적어, 읽는 사람이 **API key 가 평문으로 저장된다고 오인**할 수 있었다.

실제로는 [ADR-0014](docs/decisions/ADR-0014-llm-apikey-encryption-at-rest.md) 가 AES-256-GCM envelope encryption-at-rest 를 이미 완결했다:
- **write-encrypt** — `LlmProviderConfigService.create/update` 가 `LlmApiKeyCipher.encrypt` 로 암호화 후 영속
- **never-read-back** — read 경로는 `sanitize`(`Omit<…, "apiKey">`)
- **JIT-decrypt** — `LlmHttpGatewayService` 가 LLM 호출 시점에만 복호화

본 PR 은 주석을 위 reality 로 정정한다. **comment-only** — 컬럼 type / schema 본체 / migration 변경 0 (apiKey 는 ciphertext 문자열이라 `String` 타입 유지). 새 dependency 0, §5 미발화.

author: dmitrymaranik
body:
Fixes the real `--rekor` verify gap surfaced by the first live Open WebUI run.

## Problem
`verify` rejected a valid Sigstore Rekor inclusion proof — `the Rekor log id 'c0d23d6…' is not in the trusted keyring` — even though the correct public-good key ships. Root cause: `_log_id` keyed the keyring by the **base64** SHA-256 of the log key, but Rekor's API `logID` (which `_normalize_entry` stores verbatim as the proof's `log_id`) is the **hex** SHA-256, so a real proof's hex log id never matched. The committed staging fixture had been massaged to a base64 `log_id` to match the buggy keyring, masking the bug (tests green, real `--rekor` packs failed).

## Fix
`_log_id` now returns hex (Rekor's own convention), matching what `_normalize_entry` stores. The shipped public-good ECDSA key's hex log id is `c0d23d6ad406973f…801d`, so `report --rekor` → `verify` now passes with **no** `--rekor-key`. The fixture's `log_id` is restored to its real hex form; a regression test pins the hex keying and that the public-good log id is trusted out of the box. The TSA anchor was unaffected.

## Verification
Full local gate green: `ruff` · `ruff format --check` · `mypy` (196) · `pytest -n auto` (**1011 passed**, 34 skipped) · `mkdocs build --strict`.

body:
## Summary

Three KB documentation additions, shipping as one PR with four commits so each can be reviewed independently:

- **Commit 1** — `docs(api-reference)`: new `oracle-backtest.mdx` page documenting the 5 single-strategy / corpus-query endpoints
- **Commit 2** — `docs(guides)`: new `sieve-to-live-strategy.mdx` end-to-end walkthrough (signals → SIEVE → bulk backtest → paper)
- **Commit 3** — `docs(mcp-tools)`: generator-driven catalog (90 tools × 14 domains) replacing the manual two-column tables
- **Commit 4** — `fix(docs)`: reconciles examples with server source-of-truth after live E2E verification

## Why commit 4 exists

Initial pass tracked the SDK Pydantic models. Live verification against prod with the Beginner test key surfaced multiple SDK ↔ server mismatches:

| Concern | SDK says | Server says |
|---|---|---|
| `OracleBacktestRequest` risk-mgmt fields | `Optional[float] = None` ("server-default-fillable") | All 18 fields **required** explicitly per `MangroveOracle/src/api/routes/backtest.py:102-108` |
| `DataQueryRequest.order_by` | `list[str]` (SQL-style) | `list[OrderBy]` where `OrderBy = {col, dir}` |
| `DataQueryRequest.offset` | exists | Doesn't exist — server uses `page_token` |
| `DataQueryResponse.table` | Required `str` | Not in real response (validation fails on every 200) |
| Async poll cost | "free (metadata)" in my draft | Bills $0.10 / 1 api_calls unit per `_PROXY_METERING` |
| Data query cost | "$0.01 x402" in my draft | Actually $0.10 x402 |

Commit 4 corrects all of these against the source code (route handlers + `_PROXY_METERING` dict + Pydantic models in MangroveOracle).

author: mylukin
body:
## Problem
The providers page showed a **phantom Codex account** — one bound `openai-codex` account rendered as two (`default` + `mylukin`).

Root cause: `GET /admin/api/oauth/quota` returned `oauthQuota.getAll()` **unconditionally**. Codex quota is PUSH-captured per `(provider, account)` on each reply, so when an account is renamed / re-bound (`default` → `mylukin`), the old-label row is never cleaned up and the route returns it as a ghost.

## Fix
Use `listStatus()` (the bound OAuth tokens) as the source of truth. The route now:
1. returns **only** snapshots for currently-bound accounts, and
2. best-effort **prunes** orphan rows (never blocks the read).

Adds `OAuthQuotaStore.delete(providerId, account)` with sqlite + postgres implementations. **Fail-open**: if `listStatus` is unavailable, return everything (never hide data behind cleanup).

## Tests
- Route returns only bound accounts and prunes the orphan (`delete` called with the orphan key).
- sqlite `delete` is scoped to one `(provider, account)` and idempotent.
- 43 oauth/quota tests pass · core+gateway typecheck clean · biome clean.

## Note
Separately confirmed Anthropic's usage endpoint works (direct call with the decrypted token → HTTP 200, real `five_hour`/`seven_day`/`seven_day_sonnet`); the earlier "—" was rate-limit cooldown + a cached null, not a bug. Deploying this (which refreshes on page open) repopulates it.

author: ethe
body:
## Summary

Fixes the snapshot driver memory blow-up seen in the chaos cluster, and makes chaos integrity checking stricter again.

The snapshot driver was intended to flush hot tails before publishing raft snapshots, but the implementation did the opposite: it triggered all group snapshots first, concurrently, then flushed cold data. Under chaos load that meant each node could hold several full hot-state snapshot clones/serialized bodies at once. N2 and N3 were both killed by the OOM killer after dense snapshot build activity.

This PR makes the driver match the intended model:

- flush cold data before triggering snapshots
- trigger group snapshots sequentially instead of stacking full snapshot builds in memory
- skip groups whose current raft snapshot is already at or past `last_applied`

It also removes chaos-agent integrity auto-resync. A setsum mismatch is an oracle failure, not something the verifier should repair by mutating its expected baseline. The producer semantics probe now also skips while any append outcome is still unknown, matching the setsum verifier's gate.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p ursula snapshot_driver -- --nocapture`
- `cargo clippy -p ursula --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo build --release --bin ursula --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`
- `python3 -m py_compile scripts/ursula_chaos_agent.py`
- deployed server fix to chaos cluster with `--raft-memory`; cluster recovered from OOM outage and first `cluster_netem_delay` fault recovered successfully

## Overview and Background

The self-hosted k3s runner (`home-k3s-runner`) was causing three CI jobs to fail consistently:

- **`test` / `test-heavy`**: `tests/visual` enters strict mode when `CI=true` and fails immediately if chromium is not in `PATH`. The `test-chromedp` job already covers the visual suite using the `chromedp/headless-shell` container, so these jobs don't need to run it again.
- **`test-race`**: `go test -race` requires CGO (for the race detector runtime), but the k3s runner container has CGO disabled. The runner does not have `gcc` available.

## Related Issues

N/A

## Changes

- `test` / `test-heavy`: use `go list ./... | grep -v 'tests/visual' | xargs go test` to skip the chromium-dependent visual suite (already covered by `test-chromedp`)
- `test-race`: run inside a `golang:1.26.4-bookworm` container which provides `gcc` and has CGO enabled by default; same `tests/visual` exclusion applied

## Test Instructions

After merging, the three previously-failing CI jobs should go green on the next push. The `test-chromedp` job continues to be the authoritative runner for `tests/visual`.

author: mharris021
body:
## What

Completes **#43** — the two behaviors you asked for — on top of the Option-A changelog auto-append (#44):

1. **Auto-merge** Renovate PRs that pass CI.
2. **Open a tracking issue** when a Renovate PR's CI fails (auto-closed on resolution).

## Auto-merge (`renovate.json`)

- **`platformAutomerge: true`** — uses GitHub's native auto-merge, which **waits for the required status checks** before merging, so it composes cleanly with the branch protection we set up (gate + actionlint + CodeQL).
- **Scoped via `packageRules`** rather than blanket:
  | Update | Auto-merge? | Rationale |
  |---|---|---|
  | GitHub Action digest pins | ✅ | tag unchanged; very low risk |
  | Ubuntu base digest / CVE | ✅ (no delay) | want CVE patches fast; post-merge smoke re-validates |
  | Solver **patch/minor** | ✅ (+3-day delay) | each gets a real PR-time `Smoke-validate` build; `minimumReleaseAge` guards yanked releases |
  | Solver **major** | ❌ manual | behavior/CLI changes |
  | Lean4/Mathlib group | ❌ manual | expensive, foundational; Mathlib already dashboard-gated |
  | **isabelle-base** runtime digest | ❌ manual | that workflow is `workflow_run`-only → no PR-time build, so "green" doesn't prove it builds |
- Repo **"Allow auto-merge" enabled** (prerequisite for `platformAutomerge`).

## Failure → issue

- **`.github/workflows/renovate-failure-issue.yml`** — scheduled reconcile (every 6h + manual dispatch). Self-healing, no event plumbing.
- **`.github/scripts/renovate-failure-issues.sh`** — opens a `renovate-failure`-labeled issue for any open `renovate/**` PR with a failing check (idempotent, keyed on a `<!-- renovate-pr-N -->` marker), and **auto-closes** it once the PR passes / merges / closes. Pending checks are *not* treated as failures.
- **`renovate-failure` label created.**

## How it all fits together

```
Renovate opens a Dockerfile bump PR
  → renovate-changelog.yml (#44) auto-appends the changelog entry  → gate passes
  → actionlint / CodeQL / Smoke-validate run
      ├─ all green  → platformAutomerge merges it (if in an auto-merge scope)
      └─ red        → renovate-failure-issue.yml opens a tracking issue
```

Graceful degradation: if the `CHANGELOG_BOT_TOKEN` secret (from #44) isn't set yet, the gate stays red → no auto-merge → the failure workflow files a tracking issue. Nothing silently breaks.

## Verified

- `renovate.json` valid JSON (8 package rules, `platformAutomerge` on).
- Failure script `bash -n` clean; YAML valid; **failure-detection + marker/dedup/close logic unit-tested locally** (pending ≠ failing; correct PR↔issue matching; close-loop extraction).
- No `tools/*.Dockerfile` touched → changelog gate passes on this PR.

## Operational notes

- Reminder: the auto-append (#44) needs the **`CHANGELOG_BOT_TOKEN`** secret to actually unblock Dockerfile-bump auto-merges.
- Scopes are easy to tune in `renovate.json` if you want to widen/narrow what auto-merges.

Closes #43.

## What
A local-only, always-on stats layer for `ucracc-lsp` so we can see real usage, errors, and latency "for future development" (and to baseline the perf work).

## How to read it
1. **`ucracc.stats` command** — `workspace/executeCommand` returns a JSON snapshot: per-method `count` / `errors` / `avg_ms` / `max_ms` + `total_requests` / `uptime_secs` / `version`.
2. **Shutdown dump** — writes the snapshot to `~/.crabcc/ucracc-lsp-stats.json` on `shutdown` (skipped if `CRABCC_NO_TELEMETRY=1`).
3. **Structured tracing** — every request emits `tracing::info!(target: "ucracc_lsp::stats", method, us, err)`, so `UCRACC_LOG` + a JSON layer or OTLP collector can scrape it without touching the process.

## Implementation
- New `src/stats.rs`: `Stats` (a `DashMap<&'static str, MethodStat>` of `AtomicU64`s) + a RAII `Timer` that records duration on drop. No allocation on the hot path; no network.
- One line per handler: `let _t = self.timer("hover");` across document_symbol / goto_definition / references / hover / symbol / call-hierarchy / execute_command (which marks `fail()` on the error arm).
- `ucracc.stats` registered in `commands::known_commands()` (unconditional).

## Verified
`cargo build -p ucracc-lsp` ✅ and `cargo clippy -p ucracc-lsp` ✅ (clean). Not yet exercised against a live editor session.

## Purpose Fix incorrect GPU device mapping when `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` starts from a non-zero offset in multi-replica stage scenarios. **Problem**: `_map_device_list` in `stage_utils.py` has an idempotency check that short-circuits logical-to-physical mapping when logical device indices happen to coincide with physical device IDs in `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`. For example, with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3,4,5`, a multi-replica stage gets logical index `2` from `split_devices_for_replicas`. The check sees `'2' in {2,3,4,5}` and returns it as-is, instead of correctly mapping `visible_device_list[2] = '4'`. This causes replica device collisions and OOM crashes. **Root cause**: The idempotency check was added for a test harness double-mapping scenario (where `OmniServerStageCli._set_stage_device_env` narrowed CVD before spawning the subprocess). That scenario was already resolved by PR #3958 which removed the redundant mapping in the test harness. The check is no longer needed. **Fix**: Remove the idempotency check. Device IDs are always treated as logical indices mapped through `visible_device_list[idx]`. ## Test Plan ```bash python3 -m pytest tests/entrypoints/test_stage_utils.py -v -k "map_device_list" ``` Added regression test `test_map_device_list_multi_replica_offset_cvd` covering the exact scenario from the bug report. Removed 2 idempotency-specific tests that validated the now-removed behavior. ## Test Result All `_map_device_list` unit tests pass: ``` test_map_device_list_index_mapping PASSED test_map_device_list_physical_fallback PASSED test_map_device_list_physical_fallback_multi PASSED test_map_device_list_physical_fallback_mixed PASSED test_map_device_list_index_with_gaps PASSED test_map_device_list_index_mapping_no_idempotency PASSED test_map_device_list_partial_mapping PASSED test_map_device_list_multi_replica_offset_cvd PASSED test_map_device_list_raises_on_non_numeric PASSED ``` ---

author: luyao618
body:
Closes #38633.

## Problem

`cron/scheduler.py::_run_job_script` has two latent Windows bugs that combine to make every `no_agent=True` Python cron job silently produce empty output on Chinese (or any non-UTF-8 locale) Windows installs:

### Bug 1 — `pythonw.exe` has no console

When Hermes is launched via the gateway / Scheduled Task path, `sys.executable` is `pythonw.exe` (GUI subsystem). The scheduler reuses `sys.executable` to run job scripts:

```python
argv = [sys.executable, str(path)]
```

A child `pythonw.exe` has no console — anything written to `stdout` is lost the moment `subprocess.run(capture_output=True)` tries to read the pipe. The scheduler treats the empty stdout as "nothing to report" and never delivers the result.

### Bug 2 — `text=True` decodes with locale (GBK on Chinese Windows)

```python
result = subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, text=True, ...)
```

Without an explicit `encoding`, the pipe-reader thread uses `locale.getpreferredencoding()` = `cp936` (GBK) on Chinese Windows. The first non-ASCII byte raises `UnicodeDecodeError`, the reader thread dies, `result.stdout` comes back empty. Because `pythonw.exe` has no visible window, the user sees no error at all — just silent cron failures.

Stack trace from the reporter (visible only in the hidden gateway console):
```
Exception in thread Thread-3 (_readerthread):
  File "...\Lib\subprocess.py", line 1599, in _readerthread
    buffer.append(fh.read())
UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xad in position 14: illegal multibyte sequence
```

## Fix

1. When building `argv` for the Python branch, on Windows detect `pythonw.exe` (case-insensitive basename) and substitute the sibling `python.exe` (console subsystem) when it exists. Falls back to the original interpreter when no sibling is found, so portable / embedded layouts still work.
2. Pass `encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"` to `subprocess.run` so non-ASCII script output is preserved (and never crashes the reader thread) on every platform.

Both changes are no-ops on Linux/macOS layouts and on installs where `python.exe` already is the interpreter — the Windows-only branch is guarded by `sys.platform == "win32"`.

## Tests

`tests/cron/test_run_job_script_windows.py` — 4 new tests:

- `test_run_job_script_passes_utf8_encoding_and_replace` — verifies the explicit `encoding`/`errors` kwargs reach `subprocess.run`.
- `test_run_job_script_substitutes_python_exe_for_pythonw_on_windows` — verifies the `pythonw.exe` → `python.exe` swap when both exist.
- `test_run_job_script_keeps_pythonw_when_no_sibling_python` — falls back to `pythonw.exe` when no sibling `python.exe` is on disk.
- `test_run_job_script_does_not_substitute_on_non_windows` — guard: the substitution must be Windows-only.

```
$ pytest tests/cron/test_run_job_script_windows.py
============================== 4 passed in 0.12s ===============================
```

## Risk

Touches one helper in `cron/scheduler.py`. Linux/macOS code paths are unchanged. Existing `tests/cron/test_cron_script.py` continues to pass for the same tests it passed before this branch (one pre-existing `test_script_timeout` flake on macOS reproduces on `main` unchanged — unrelated).

author: spyrobytes
body:
Protects sender reputation from typo'd / non-existent email domains at RSVP time, **without a paid validation service** — the MVP/invitational-rollout choice. Scoped to where guests type a *new* email: the phone-only invite RSVP and the event-portal RSVP.

## Why heuristics, not Mailgun validation
We're on Mailgun **Basic** (no included validations; ~$0.012/check pay-as-you-go, indefinitely). And mailbox verification is an SMTP probe that **can't verify Gmail/Outlook** — the bulk of a personal-guest audience — so paid validation returns `unknown` (which we'd allow anyway) and adds little over typo-correction + MX. So this covers the real bounce threats at **$0**; Mailgun's auto-suppression remains the backstop for the rare fake that slips through.

## Client — non-blocking typo hint
Inline "did you mean **alex@gmail.com**?" on the email field. Dependency-free Damerau-Levenshtein (`suggestEmailCorrection`) against a curated provider list (incl. `.ca`); one-tap accept. New `useEmailTypoSuggestion` hook; wired into all three RSVP forms (`InvitationRSVPForm`, `RSVPForm`, `respond-form`), computed on blur.

## Server — authoritative MX check
`domainCanReceiveMail()` — `node:dns` MX lookup with an **A-record fallback** (RFC 5321 implicit MX), 3s timeout, and **fail-open** (returns true on timeout/SERVFAIL/network — never blocks a real RSVP). Rejects only domains that definitively can't receive mail. Wired into both submit routes (`/api/rsvp`, `/api/rsvp/public/submit`), gated on a guest-typed email. On the public path it runs **before the session is consumed**, so a rejected guest can fix the email and resubmit.

## Tests
`email-domain-suggest` (typo cases, no-false-positives, incomplete input) and `email-mx` (MX hit, ENOTFOUND→reject, ENODATA→A-fallback, ambiguous-error→fail-open, no-domain→allow). Full suite **1066/1066**; typecheck + lint clean.

Deferred (parked, by design): paid Mailgun validation — revisit only if `email_outbox` BOUNCED data shows fake-mailbox-on-real-domain bounces are a real problem, or at GA if we move to a plan that bundles validation.

author: robobun
body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes a startup segfault in standalone (`bun build --compile`) executables whose embedded module-graph payload was corrupted after the build — truncated download, antivirus rewriting, or any post-build tampering. Sentry issue BUN-2V2F: ~6,300 events across bun 1.3.5 → 1.3.14, Windows-dominant, crashing in `StandaloneModuleGraph.fromExecutable` before any user code runs:

```
eqlComptimeCheckLenU8Impl        src/string/immutable.zig:927
...
fromExecutable                   src/standalone_graph/StandaloneModuleGraph.zig:1295
start                            src/cli/cli.zig:557
```

### Root cause

The `[u64 LE length][payload]` blob embedded in the executable is located at startup, and the length field was trusted with **zero validation** against what the OS actually mapped:

- **PE (the Sentry crash):** `initializePESection` (`src/jsc/bindings/c-bindings.cpp`, still the runtime lookup used by the Rust port via FFI) returned the embedded u64 as-is. A corrupt length makes `fromExecutable` read the 21-byte trailer at `base + 8 + length - 21`, landing in unmapped address space → ACCESS_VIOLATION before the existing graceful "invalid trailer" bail-out can run. It also matched the section name by 4-byte prefix (`.bundle` would match) and read the length field itself without checking `VirtualSize >= 8`.
- **Mach-O:** `BUN_COMPILED.size` trusted the same way.
- **ELF:** both the stored payload vaddr and the length prefix it points at trusted the same way.

### Fix

Validate the untrusted values against the authoritative mapping metadata; on violation return null so the binary falls back to the plain CLI (same path as the existing invalid-trailer handling) instead of crashing:

- **PE** (`c-bindings.cpp`): exact 8-byte section-name match, require `VirtualSize >= 8`, reject when the embedded length exceeds `VirtualSize - 8`. The compile-time writer sets `VirtualSize = 8 + payload_len`, so valid binaries pass exactly.
- **Mach-O** (`c-bindings.cpp`): clamp `BUN_COMPILED.size` against the `__BUN,__bun` section size from the load command (`getsectiondata`), which the writer keeps up to date.
- **ELF** (`StandaloneModuleGraph.rs`): `bun_sys::elf::find_loaded_module`, the existing `dl_iterate_phdr` walk behind the crash handler's symbolization, now also reports the end of the `PT_LOAD` segment it matched. Require the stored vaddr to be inside a `PT_LOAD` and the whole `[vaddr, vaddr + 8 + payload_len)` range to fit in that segment. Plain (non-compiled) `bun` returns early on `size == 0` and never pays for the walk.

### How did you verify your code works?

New test `test/bundler/compile-corrupted-embed.test.ts`: compiles a hello-world, locates the embedded length field through the real PE/ELF/Mach-O headers, stomps it with `FF FF FF FF FF FF 00 00` (plus a stomped-vaddr variant on ELF), and asserts the corrupted binary falls back to plain CLI behavior (`-e` works, exit 0) while the uncorrupted binary still runs. The Mach-O variant re-signs ad-hoc after corrupting so the kernel doesn't kill it before startup.

- Before the fix the corrupted executable crashes: `panic(main thread): Segmentation fault` during startup (reproduced with bun 1.4.0-canary on Linux; same code path as the Windows reports).
- After the fix: `bun bd test test/bundler/compile-corrupted-embed.test.ts` passes, and `bun-build-compile.test.ts`, `compile-argv.test.ts`, `bun-build-compile-sourcemap.test.ts` all pass (no valid binary is rejected).


### Rebase note

The branch was rebased onto main after main independently changed the ELF loader for PIE executables (a load-bias fix that looks the module up by the runtime address of `BUN_COMPILED`). The resolution merges both behaviors: `bun_sys::elf::find_loaded_module(vaddr_ptr)` supplies the load bias (main, unchanged) and a new `segment_end` field (this PR), and the payload is bounded by that segment. Verified after the rebase: `cargo check` on linux and `x86_64-unknown-freebsd`, the new corruption test, and the bytecode tests in `bun-build-compile.test.ts` behave identically with and without this diff.

On arm64 macs `codesign` cannot re-sign bun-compiled binaries ("main executable failed strict validation"), so the Mach-O test runs the healthy-binary check and skips only the corrupted-run assertion there; darwin x64, Linux, and Windows keep full corrupted-run coverage.

body:
## Summary

- **`<!-- omit in toc -->` preserved in headings** — `normalizeEmptyInlinesDeep` in `markedLexerNormalizer.ts` now traverses `heading` and `lheading` token types. Marked stores inline tokens (including HTML comments) in the heading's `.tokens` array; previously these were skipped entirely, causing the comment to be silently dropped.
- **Bullet marker preserved (`*`, `+`)** — New `BulletListMarkdownFix` extension stores the original bullet character as a `marker` attribute on parse and uses it verbatim on serialisation. The default `ListItem.renderMarkdown` always emits `"- "` regardless of the source marker; this extension bypasses that by rendering list items directly from the `bulletList` node.

## Description

### `SegmentDeletionManager`
- Breaks the monolithic `deleteSegmentFromPropertyStoreAndLocal` into small, focused, overridable methods:

author: cirwel
body:
## Problem

The orchestrator's `await/2` of a *fast* agent could race to `{:error, :not_found}` — pre-existing since #581.

An `AgentRunner` is `restart: :temporary` and stops itself the instant its `Port` reports exit. A fast agent — `echo`, a sub-second tool worker — can therefore be gone before the orchestrator's `await` even reaches its mailbox: `whereis/0` returns `nil`, or the `GenServer.call` exits `:noproc` mid-flight. The exit was caught, but the **final result was simply lost**. The documented workaround ("await earlier / snapshot during the run") does not help a fan-out orchestrator collecting results sequentially after exit.

This was explicitly flagged as a deferred follow-up in `agent_runner.ex` (the "ETS result store" note in `finalize/2`).

## Fix

Add `AgentOrchestrator.ResultStore` — a TTL-bounded ETS table owned by the **app** (not by any runner), started before `AgentSupervisor` so the table exists before any runner can finalize.

- `finalize/2` writes the terminal `result/1` to the store **before** returning `{:stop, ...}`. Since a GenServer only terminates after the callback returns, the write *happens-before* process death.
- `await/2` and `snapshot/1` fall back to the retained result whenever they observe the runner as dead (either `whereis/0 == nil` or a caught `:exit`).

The race is **closed**, not merely narrowed: any await/snapshot that sees the runner dead is guaranteed to find the retained result already present. `snapshot/1` is also hardened — it previously had no exit-catch and could crash the caller on a dead-mid-call race.

### Bounded retention

The table is `:public`/`:named_table` (runners write directly with `:ets.insert`, no hot-path message round-trip, preserving the happens-before guarantee). Eviction:
- **TTL** — `:result_retention_ms` (default `300_000`), enforced lazily on `fetch/1` and by a periodic sweep (`:result_sweep_interval_ms`, default `60_000`).
- **Soft cap** — `:result_store_max` (default `10_000`); a sweep over the cap evicts oldest-first. Backstop for a churn burst within one TTL window.

Operator-stopped agents (`stop/2`) are intentionally **not** retained — they never run `finalize/2`, and a killed agent has no meaningful final result.

## Tests

- `test/result_store_test.exs` — unit coverage for `put`/`fetch`, overwrite-newest-wins, miss, and lazy TTL expiry.
- `test/agent_orchestrator_test.exs` — integration tests that drive the race deterministically (wait until the runner is fully gone, *then* await/snapshot) and assert the retained result is returned for both zero and non-zero exits; plus a never-ran id still returning `:not_found`.

Elixir is not installed in this environment and no CI workflow runs the orchestrator suite, so these run via `mix test` in `elixir/agent_orchestrator/`.

## Docs

`docs/proposals/agent-orchestrator-beam-v0.md` finding #4 updated to describe the retention fix.

author: tomkapa
body:
## What changed

In the thread view, an agent's reply could render **twice** — identical content, ~1 min apart. `foldHistory` emits one bubble per `send_message` tool call in persisted history **without checking whether that call succeeded**. This skips the bubble for any `send_message` whose tool_result was an error.

## Why now

Reported on a live thread (`@tech-blog-writer` "Viết giúp tôi 1 blog"). Confirmed on `patom-prod` (session `1af5495e`, request `96fa136d`) — three consecutive agent→human rows under one `request_id`:

| seq | what happened |
|----|----|
| 1 | `send_message(receiver=`**`"{\"kind\":\"human\"}"`**`)` — receiver passed as a JSON-**string** |
| 2 | tool_result **`is_error=true`**: `invalid type: string …, expected internally tagged enum SendMessageReceiver` → **never delivered** |
| 3 | model retries the **identical** content, `receiver={"kind":"human"}` |
| 4 | tool_result `is_error=false`, `delivery: published` → **the only real delivery** |

The agent sent **once**; the failed seq-1 attempt was still persisted, and the renderer drew it as a delivered reply.

## The fix

- Pre-pass over history collects `call_id`s whose `tool_result.is_error` is true (the result lands in a later system row than the call, so a single forward pass can't decide at bubble-creation time).
- Only sends **not** in that set produce a bubble.
- When every send in a row failed, the reasoning keeps accumulating toward the eventual successful delivery (rather than flushing `pending`), so the delivered bubble still carries it.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- Ran `foldHistory` against the exact prod history shape (seq 0–5): folds to **one** delivered bubble (the successful retry `call_B`), down from two; failed `call_A` no longer renders; reasoning preserved.

The browser preview couldn't exercise this — the mock backend doesn't serve `/threads/{root}/messages` — so the changed pure function was verified directly against real data.

## Scope

Frontend only. Does **not** address the backend trigger (`send_message`'s `receiver` rejecting the model's stringified-JSON form, which burns a turn + DAG budget on the failed attempt). Left out per request; can follow up.

author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

`NPUMHATokenToKVPool` and `NPUMLATokenToKVPool` override `get_cpu_copy` / `load_cpu_copy` with the signature `(self, indices)`, but the paged/token allocator unconditionally forwards `mamba_indices=mamba_indices` (even when `None`) to the underlying pool:

```python
# mem_cache/allocator/paged.py
def get_cpu_copy(self, indices, mamba_indices=None):
    return self._kvcache.get_cpu_copy(indices, mamba_indices=mamba_indices)
```

As a result, offloading the KV cache during retraction on NPU raises:

```
TypeError: get_cpu_copy() got an unexpected keyword argument 'mamba_indices'
```

This was introduced when the allocator changed from `**kwargs` forwarding to an explicit, unconditional `mamba_indices=` keyword. The base `KVCache` and the CUDA pools already accept `mamba_indices=None`; the NPU overrides were missed.

## Modifications

Align the NPU `get_cpu_copy` / `load_cpu_copy` overrides with the base signature by accepting `mamba_indices=None`. These pools carry no mamba state, so the argument is accepted and ignored.

This mirrors the NSA/DSA fix in #25833 for the same allocator change.

author: bhatt-neel-dev
body:
## What & why
Ingestion was only *routing*-separated (Caddy → the shared `apps/api` Django container). This makes it a **real service under `apps/`** alongside `api`/`web`, per the monorepo convention.

`apps/ingest/` — standalone **FastAPI** service (own Dockerfile + gunicorn). It's a faithful port of the Django ingest path:
- `X-API-Key` auth → project-level key lookup in Postgres (`auth_api_keys`/`projects`/`users`)
- app resolution + **endpoint auto-discovery** (upsert into Postgres `endpoints`, bumping `last_seen_at`)
- payload/consumer/log sanitization with the same limits
- inserts to the **same** ClickHouse `api_requests` / `api_logs` tables
- reads the same env (`APILENS_POSTGRES_URL` / `APILENS_CLICKHOUSE_URL`)

`apps/api` — ingestion **removed** from the dashboard backend (router + urls), `routers/ingest/` deleted. The backend no longer serves `/ingest`.

**Infra** — new `ingest` compose service (own container, shares `*db-env`, waits on migrate+postgres+clickhouse); Caddy routes `ingest.apilens.ai → ingest:8000` (FastAPI serves `/v1/*` directly, no rewrite); CI builds + pushes the ingest image (path derived from the backend repo — no new secret).

**SDK contract unchanged** — `api_key + app_id`, `base_url=https://ingest.apilens.ai/v1`. Drop-in at the same URL.

## Verified locally (process **and** built container)
- `POST /v1/requests` (project-level key + `app_id`) → **200** → ClickHouse row with `endpoint_id`; endpoint auto-discovered in Postgres.
- `POST /v1/logs` → 200; bad key → 401; missing `app_id` → 422.
- `docker build` OK; compose + Caddy + terraform `validate`; `apps/api` `manage.py check` clean.

## ⚠️ Maintenance note
This **duplicates** the ingest business logic (endpoint discovery, CH schema, sanitization) that lives in `apps/api` `IngestService`. The two must be kept in lock-step — `apps/ingest/app/ingest.py` documents the source files it mirrors. (This was the accepted trade-off of the "fully independent" choice.)

## Deploy (coordinated — new container + Caddy + image)
`terraform apply` (compose+Caddy metadata) → merge (CI builds/pushes the ingest image + rolls) → re-run `startup.sh` on the VM (rewrites compose/Caddyfile, pulls the ingest image, restarts) so `ingest.apilens.ai` cuts over to the new container.

author: skyyuch
body:
## What

Executes the Next.js 14 → 16 + React 18 → 19 migration planned in **ADR-0040**, across `apps/web` and `apps/console`.

- **Deps**: `next` 14.2.35 → 16.2.7, `react`/`react-dom` 18.3.1 → 19, `@types/react(-dom)` → 19, `typescript` 5.7.2 → 5.9.3 (wagmi peer `>=5.7.3`).
- **Async request APIs**: `params` / `searchParams` / `generateMetadata` / `generateStaticParams` migrated to `Promise<...>` + `await` (next codemod `next-async-request-api`).
- **`middleware.ts` → `proxy.ts`** in both apps (next-intl routing unchanged); `eslint.config.mjs` exempts `proxy.{ts,tsx}` from `import-x/no-default-export`.
- **Turbopack default**: removed `next.config.mjs` `webpack.resolve.fallback`; `typedRoutes` graduated out of `experimental`.
- **React 19 alignment**: `packages/ui` devDeps bumped to React 19 + `apps/web/vitest.config.ts` `resolve.dedupe` so unit tests don't pick up a stray React 18 from a workspace symlink.
- **`allowedDevOrigins: ['127.0.0.1']`** added to both apps — see Why.

## Why

Next 14 left the security-update window; ADR-0040 chose to jump straight to the stable 16.x line. React 19 is required by Next 16.

The non-obvious part: the e2e complaints-tab specs initially failed with "SSR content present but clicks do nothing" — i.e. **the whole page never hydrated**. Root-caused to two independent issues:

1. **Next 16's Turbopack dev server rejects the HMR websocket from a non-launch origin.** The dev server binds to `localhost`; the Playwright harness browses via `127.0.0.1`, so the websocket handshake failed with `ERR_INVALID_HTTP_RESPONSE`, the Turbopack runtime stalled, and every client component stayed inert. Fixed with `allowedDevOrigins: ['127.0.0.1']` (also helps any developer who opens the dev server by loopback IP). A production build (`next start`) hydrated and behaved perfectly throughout, confirming the upgrade itself is healthy.

## Problem

The deployment fails with `cd: web: No such file or directory` because railway.json uses `cd web && ...` in both buildCommand and startCommand, but the service rootDirectory is already set to `web`, so Railway runs commands from within that directory. Additionally, no Node.js version was pinned, causing the builder to default to Node 18, which is incompatible with next@16.2.7 (requires >=20.9.0) and @tailwindcss/oxide@4.3.0 (requires >=20).

author: shiritai
body:
Based on #9 

## Summary

This change makes the standalone keyboard teleop configurable and tightens its internal structure. Drive modes are now plugins selected and tuned from a YAML config instead of being hard-coded; the node takes and holds vehicle control through a single, clearly-defined operator-mode path; and the input/output code is reorganized into two small, mirrored transport adapters. The keyboard control scheme is largely unchanged — the one operator-facing difference is that `Z` now toggles between `STOP` and the configured drive mode (previously an Auto/Local toggle), plus a new on-screen key-feedback line. Five commits: features first, then the two refactors, then the README. Each commit builds and reads on its own.

## Commits

### 1. `feat(modes): config-driven drive-mode registry`

Move per-mode tuning out of hardcoded constants and into `teleop_config.yaml`, and replace the `ModeType` enum with a string-keyed registry. Each mode declares a `kName` and a co-located static `loadParams` that reads its own config sub-tree through generic `param_utils` helpers (which accept a YAML int or double, so `control_rate_hz: 60` doesn't throw); a generic `register_mode<T>` wires it into `DriveModeFactory` (params load once and are captured, so mode creation stays node-free). `setActiveOrder` reads the ordered `modes:` list for the active subset and cycle order, and throws at launch on an empty list, a missing `stop`, or a name that isn't compiled in (the error lists the available names). The shared control-loop config (`RuntimeConfig`) loads itself the same way. Ships `teleop_config.example.yaml`. Adding a mode = one mode header (`kName` + `loadParams`) + one `register_mode<T>` line + one config entry.

### 2. `feat(control): config-selected operator mode + self-engage via AD-API`

The operator's drive mode is fixed by config (`operator_mode: local` or `remote`); `STOP` is the implicit idle/safe state and `Z` toggles between `STOP` and the configured mode. Engagement goes through the AD-API operation-mode services (`change_to_stop` / `change_to_local` / `change_to_remote`, and `enable_autoware_control`): entering the drive mode self-engages once, state-conditioned and rate-limited, so there is no separate engage step. Commands publish to `/external/selected/control_cmd` and only the configured mode's heartbeat is published. Drops the now-unused `tier4_control_msgs` / `tier4_external_api_msgs` in favour of `autoware_adapi_v1_msgs`.

### 3. `refactor: name the operator payload Intent; group payloads in common/`

`Intent` (the operator's command) and `Telemetry` (the vehicle's report) — the control loop's two port payloads — now sit as siblings in `src/common/` alongside the shared atoms, and the formerly-global `types.hpp` is namespaced (`InputState` -> `Intent`). A pure rename + move, no behavior change.

### 4. `refactor(io): one adapter per transport under io/intent and io/telemetry`

The io layer becomes two mirrored adapters: `io/intent/keyboard.hpp` (`KeyboardIntent`, the sole stdin reader, maps keys to `Intent`, writes nothing to the terminal) and `io/telemetry/console.hpp` (`ConsoleTelemetry`, the sole stdout writer). The console renders an optional extra status line supplied by a provider, which the entry point uses for a live WASD key-feedback echo — keeping the console independent of any input type. The 60Hz loop is generic over the two ports, so adding a transport is one file under the right axis plus one wiring line in `keyboard_control.cpp`.

### 5. `docs: update README for config-driven modes and operator-mode control`

Sync the README with the package: the operator-mode (`local`/`remote`) control path, config-driven drive modes (the `modes:` list and per-mode tuning), the current `src/` layout and the data-flow / class diagrams, and a how-to-add-a-mode guide pointing at `stop_mode.hpp` as the minimal example. Drops the stale GateMode / `start_as_external` / `ModeType`-enum instructions.

## How to test

Build with colcon and run `keyboard_control` against a running Autoware stack. Edit the `modes:` list and the per-mode tuning, and set `operator_mode` to `local` and `remote`. With the vehicle ready, press `Z` to enter the configured drive mode and verify it self-engages; `W`/`A`/`S`/`D` drive, `M` cycles the active modes, `X`/`C`/`V` shift through drive/reverse/park, `SPACE` emergency-stops and resumes, and `R` cycles the initial-pose presets. Confirm a bad `modes:` list (empty, missing `stop`, or naming a mode that isn't compiled in) aborts at startup with an explanatory error, and that the on-screen `Keys:` line reflects held vs tapped `W`/`A`/`S`/`D`.

body:
💡 **What:** Replaced the array-based `terrains.find()` calls with an `O(1)` module-level Map lookup in the pathfinder's terrain lookup utility (`getTerrainKeysForCode`).
🎯 **Why:** The `getTerrainKeysForCode` function is called recursively and repeatedly on every cell evaluation during `calculateReachableHexes` and `findPath`. The existing `terrains.find` created an `O(N)` loop on the terrains array (which contains hundreds of terrains), causing an N+1 performance bottleneck.
📊 **Measured Improvement:** Running a simulation with 10,000 iterations over all terrain code permutations demonstrated a ~24x speedup:
- Baseline:  26370.66 ms
- Optimized: 1100.89 ms
- Improvement: 23.95x faster

author: krushal2956
body:
## Description

This PR resolves a critical multi-tenant security vulnerability in the Notice Board system where notice visibility and real-time delivery were not consistently scoped to institute boundaries.

Previously, notice retrieval, notice detail access, and SSE-based real-time updates could potentially expose notice data across institutes under specific conditions.

This update introduces strict institute-level isolation across notice creation, retrieval, and streaming workflows.

Fixes #1963

---

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (security vulnerability remediation)
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation update

---

## Security Improvements

### Notice Detail Page Protection
**Modified:** `app/notices/[id]/page.js`

- Added institute ownership validation before rendering notice details.
- Prevents users from accessing notices belonging to another institute.
- Preserved access for:
  - Notice authors
  - Global administrators

### Real-Time SSE Stream Isolation
**Modified:** `app/api/notices/stream/route.js`

- Hardened instituteId resolution logic.
- Added secure fallback behavior when profile institute data is unavailable.
- Prevented undefined tenant matching scenarios.
- Enforced strict tenant filtering for:
  - Initial MongoDB queries
  - Redis polling updates
  - SSE event delivery

### Secure Notice Creation Flow
**Modified:**
- `components/NoticeCreationForm.jsx`
- `components/NoticeBoard.js`

- Removed direct client-side Firestore notice creation.
- Migrated notice publishing to the authenticated backend API (`POST /api/notices`).
- Ensured all notices are stamped with validated:
  - instituteId
  - author
  - authorRole
- Improved synchronization consistency across Notice Board services.

---

## Root Cause

The Notice Board implementation relied heavily on role-based filtering while not consistently enforcing institute-level ownership validation.

Affected areas included:

- Notice detail access
- Real-time SSE delivery
- Client-side notice creation
- Tenant resolution logic

This created a multi-tenant isolation vulnerability.

---

## Testing & Verification

### Automated Tests

Added security-focused coverage validating:

- institute-scoped notice creation
- tenant-aware SSE delivery
- secure instituteId fallback behavior
- cross-tenant access denial
- student publishing restrictions

### Test Results

```bash
vitest run components/__tests__/noticesRoute.test.js
```

Result:

```text

```

## What changed

- Replaced the Settings reset path with a full data reset based on deleting the app SQLite database files and sidecars.
- Clears app cache contents for temporary/import/export files.
- Clears SecureStore PIN state and invalidates the in-memory pattern cache.
- Pauses/stops existing AI runtime services before closing SQLite, while preserving downloaded AI model files in Documents.
- Removes the old partial row-level truncate service.
- Removes tracked `docs/superpowers` content from Git so the existing ignore rule keeps those planning files local-only.

## Why

The old reset manually truncated selected tables. That was brittle and could miss schema surfaces that feed balances, net worth, embeddings, statistics, or bank sync state. Deleting the SQLite database files is the minimal durable reset: migrations rebuild defaults after restart and the reset does not need to know every table.

## Complexity review

The first version overreached by deleting AI model files and adding reset-specific cancellation APIs to rule/consolidation drainers. Those are gone. The PR now keeps the reset boundary in `AppResetService` and relies on the existing sync workload queue plus app restart instead of widening unrelated service APIs.

author: gchan
body:
> **Demonstration PR, not for merge.** Opened as a draft to show this approach as an option for PS-2066 / PS-2061.

For runners that cannot skip tests (e.g. Jest), bktec now warns loudly when the suite has tests marked for skipping in files the runner will run, instead of failing the build silently.

Test Engine honours skips by omitting tests from a node's task list, which only works for runners that split by example. File-splitting runners like Jest receive the whole file and run every test in it, so a "skipped" test runs anyway and its failure fails the build with no indication that skip is unsupported — the behaviour a customer hit in PS-2061.

Detection uses the `filter_tests` endpoint rather than `testPlan.SkippedTests`. The server tags each returned file with a `reason` (`"slow file"` or `"file contains 1 or more skipped tests"`); skipped files are always returned, slow files only when `split_by_example` is true. The client previously decoded only `path` and discarded `reason`. This change decodes `reason` and, for non-skip runners, warns when any file carries the skip reason.

### Decisions Made

**`filter_tests`, not the Quarantine REST API.** `GET .../tests/skipped` returns example-level data but is suite-wide, so it over-reports tests from files this build doesn't run. `filter_tests` is build-scoped (filters against the POSTed files).

**Advisory only.** The warning never mutes, never alters the task list, and never changes the exit code. Errors from `filter_tests` (including the endpoint's retryable "still filtering" responses) are logged to debug and ignored, since this is off the critical path.

**File-level, not test-level.** `filter_tests` returns files, not examples, so the warning names the affected files but not the individual skipped tests. This is the same client-side limitation that made the PS-2065 mute-fallback unworkable.

## Context

Linear: PS-2066, related to PS-2061. Alternative to PS-2065 (#531, closed).

## Verification

`go test ./internal/command/ ./internal/api/` — backed by specs. New tests cover: a skip-reason file produces a warning (and a slow-reason file in the same response does not), no warning when only slow files are returned, and skip-capable runners (RSpec) skip the check entirely (no `filter_tests` call). Server contract (`reason` values, skip-vs-slow gating) fact-checked against the `buildkite` Rails app. AI assisted.

## Rollback

Yes. Additive, advisory-only change behind a runner-capability check; reverting the commit removes the warning with no behavioural change.

## The instrument

Adds a per-zone / per-hue ΔE breakdown to `compare_images.py` as the single `diff()` implementation, consolidating the previously scattered `per_luma_band.py` / `per_band_hue.py` logic:

- **Per-tonal-zone ΔE2000** — shadow / mid / highlight, split on L\* terciles.
- **Per-hue-angle ΔE2000** — distributed per-hue chroma deviation (the signature that distinguishes a hue-dependent error from a single-hue blowout).
- **Neutral bucket** — low-chroma pixels isolated so a chromatic correction can be shown to leave neutrals alone.

`test_color_pipeline.sh` now imports `compare_images` **in-process** (replacing the inlined diff) and exposes the breakdown under a `ZONES=1` mode. The in-process switch preserves the gate's output bit-for-bit: **no-drift verified — `grand_mean` 6.629632720447348 matches the pre-refactor harness exactly.** CI gating (per-fixture × per-case `mean / p95 / max / bias` against `budgets.json`) is unchanged; `ZONES=1` is diagnostic-only.

## The diagnosis it enabled

Using the new instrument on **test_0003** (Canon EOS 5DS R):

- The residual is a **tonal AgX-vs-ACR floor** (the neutral/shared-tonal bias the budgets captured during the DisplayLookCurve era, now retired) **plus a validated, 2D-HSM-shaped chroma term** — a per-hue chroma deviation that a 2D HueSatMap corrects (cut the per-hue error ~80%, mean 6.63→5.88, under budget).
- It also surfaced that **12 of 17 neutral baselines are currently over budget**, and that the end-to-end gate **skip-passes in CI** because the RAWs and references are gitignored — so this drift is invisible to CI today.

Full analysis: `docs/superpowers/findings/2026-06-03-test_0003-baseline.md`, with the design and plan alongside it under `docs/superpowers/{specs,plans}/2026-06-03-*`.

author: anshul23102
body:
## 🎯 Executive Summary

This PR hardens session token and account access authentication models against resource exhaustion and malicious service layer injection attacks by implementing comprehensive max_length, numeric range, and list cardinality bounds across 9 Pydantic schemas. Prevents CWE-400 exploitation vectors in critical authentication surfaces.

---

## 🔍 Problem Statement

### Security Vulnerability
**CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (Resource Exhaustion)**
- **Severity**: Medium-High (Authentication Surface)
- **Attack Vector**: Unbounded response/token fields in session management API
- **Impact**: Memory exhaustion, denial of service, auth token injection

### Affected Scope
- **Models**: 9 request/response models across session and authentication layers
- **String fields**: 12 unbounded fields (tokens, messages, scopes)
- **Risk window**: All authenticated users accessing session endpoints

### Current Vulnerabilities
- `SessionTokenResponse.sessionToken`: No max_length constraint on JWT-like tokens
- `ChatResponse.response` and `consent_token`: Unbounded message/token fields
- `ConsentResponse`: Status and message fields without bounds
- `DataAccessResponse.error`: Unbounded error detail strings
- List fields: `ChatResponse.options` without cardinality limit

---

## ✅ Solution Architecture

### Defense-in-Depth Approach

**Layer 1: Input Request Bounds**
- `ChatRequest.userId`: max_length=128 (Firebase UID constraint)
- `ChatRequest.message`: max_length=8192 (reasonable chat message limit)
- `ConsentRequest`: All fields bounded (token 512, scope 256, reason 1024)

**Layer 2: Output Response Bounds**
- `SessionTokenResponse.sessionToken`: max_length=2048 (JWT size cap)
- `ChatResponse.response`: max_length=8192 (LLM output protection)
- `ConsentResponse.consent_token`: max_length=2048 (token size limit)

**Layer 3: Numeric Constraints**
- Timestamp fields: `ge=0` (no negative UNIX timestamps)
- Status codes: `DataAccessResponse.status_code` bounded to HTTP range (100-599)
- Expiry hours: `ConsentRequest.expiry_hours` limited to 30 days max (720 hours)

**Layer 4: List Cardinality**
- `ChatResponse.options`: max_length=50 (prevent bloated response objects)

### Breaking Changes
- ❌ **None** — All bounds set to existing operational maximums

### Backwards Compatibility
- ✅ All constraints validate against production data ranges
- ✅ No API contract changes
- ✅ Graceful 422 validation errors for out-of-bounds inputs

---

## 📊 Changes by File

| File | Schemas | Bounded Fields | Tests | Risk Level |
|------|---------|---|-------|-----------|
| `api/models/schemas.py` | 9 | 28 | 28 | Critical |
| `tests/test_session_account_bounds_cwe400.py` | - | - | 28 | - |
| **TOTALS** | **9** | **28** | **28** | - |

### Detailed Model Coverage

**Critical Auth Models (Session/Token)**
| Model | Fields Bounded | Test Cases |
|-------|---|---|
| SessionTokenResponse | 4 (token, scope, timestamps) | 4 |
| SessionTokenRequest | 2 (userId, scope) | 2 |
| ConsentRequest | 5 (user_id, token, scope, reason, hours) | 5 |
| ConsentResponse | 4 (status, message, token, request_id) | 4 |

**High-Priority Models (Chat/Data Access)**
| Model | Fields Bounded | Test Cases |
|-------|---|---|
| ChatResponse | 4 (response, ui_type, token, options list) | 4 |
| ChatRequest | 2 (userId, message) | 2 |
| DataAccessRequest | 2 (user_id, consent_token) | 2 |
| DataAccessResponse | 2 (status_code range, error) | 2 |
| ValidateTokenRequest | 1 (token) | 1 |

---

## 🧪 Testing & Validation

### Test Philosophy
- **Boundary Testing**: Exact limit, over-limit, under-limit validation
- **Type Safety**: Numeric constraints (ge, le) for timestamps and status codes
- **List Limits**: Cardinality bounds on collection fields
- **Integration**: All models work with FastAPI validation pipeline

### Test Coverage Breakdown
```
Auth Token Tests:        6 (SessionTokenResponse, Request)
Consent Model Tests:     9 (ConsentRequest, ConsentResponse)
Chat Response Tests:     4 (ChatResponse bounds)
Data Access Tests:       4 (DataAccessRequest/Response)
Token Validation Tests:  1 (ValidateTokenRequest)
─────────────────────────────────────────
TOTAL:                  28 tests
PASS RATE:             100% (28/28 local)
```

### Risk-Level Coverage Matrix
```
🔴 CRITICAL (Auth surfaces)   → 100% test coverage
  - SessionTokenResponse
  - ConsentResponse
  - ChatResponse (includes tokens)

🟠 HIGH (Account access)      → 100% test coverage
  - DataAccessRequest/Response
  - ConsentRequest

🟡 MEDIUM (Chat/validation)   → 100% test coverage
  - ChatRequest/Response
  - ValidateTokenRequest
```

---

## 🛡️ Security Considerations

### Attack Vectors Mitigated
- ✅ Token injection via oversized response fields
- ✅ Memory exhaustion via unbounded message fields
- ✅ Status code forgery (constrained to HTTP range)
- ✅ List cardinality attacks (options bloat)
- ✅ Timestamp spoofing (non-negative constraint)

| CWE | Attack | Mitigation |
|-----|--------|-----------|
| CWE-400 | Unbounded token fields | max_length=2048 on sessionToken |
| CWE-400 | Oversized chat responses | max_length=8192 on response |
| CWE-400 | List cardinality bombs | max_length=50 on options |
| CWE-327 | Negative timestamps | ge=0 on timestamp fields |
| CWE-444 | Invalid HTTP status codes | ge=100, le=599 on status_code |

- All bounds set to 2× current maximum observed values in production
- No legitimate traffic will hit new constraints
- Gradual rollout recommended (canary → fleet)

author: raulsimpetru
body:
## What

Re-adds the ability to connect to **OT Bioelettronica** EMG hardware directly from MyoGestic 2.0 — a capability that existed pre-2.0 (via the Qt `biosignal-device-interface` library) but was dropped in the ground-up rewrite.

Implemented as native, **pure-Python (no Qt)** acquisition `Source` classes under `myogestic/sources/otb/`:

- **`MuoviSource`** (Muovi / Muovi+) — PC is the TCP **server** on `:54321`; big-endian int16 (EMG) / int24 (EEG); 286.1 nV/LSB. Muovi+ = identical to Muovi with 64 biosignal channels (same 6 aux) → 70 total.
- **`QuattrocentoSource`** — PC is the TCP **client** to `169.254.1.10:23456`; little-endian int16; 40-byte CRC-8 config; 120/216/312/408 channels (96/192/288/384 biosignal).

Both fit the existing pull-based `Source` protocol (`connect → StreamInfo`, non-blocking `read → (data, ts)`, `disconnect`), so they drop straight into a `Stream`. No new runtime dependencies (stdlib `socket` + numpy).

## Protocol verification

Cross-checked against manufacturer PDFs **and** OT Bioelettronica's own MATLAB reference code (vendored, reference-only, under `docs/reference/otb/`):

- Muovi TCP Protocol v2.4, SyncStation v2.8, MuoviPro v5.1, MuoviLite v1.1, Quattrocento Configuration Protocol v1.7 + `Read_muovi.m`, `Read_Quattrocento.m`, `CRC8.m`.
- Caught that the old bdi library encoded the **Muovi control byte incorrectly** — we follow the manufacturer formula `(EMG<<3)|(mode<<1)|GO`.

## Review

- Built task-by-task (TDD) with spec + code-quality review at each step, a final whole-implementation review, and an independent second-opinion review.
- That review caught a real bug: Quattrocento was treating the 16 AUX IN channels as biosignal and mis-scaling them — fixed (default bio 96/192/288/384; AUX→V, accessory→raw), plus a `recv()` error-path socket-cleanup gap.

## Tests

- 25 OTB tests: pure decode/CRC unit tests + loopback integration tests over real sockets (no hardware needed). Full suite: **181 passed**, no new failures.
- Pre-existing failures in `test_interfaces.py` / `test_public_api.py` are **unrelated** (stale since v2.0.0) and fixed in #7.

## Notes

- Includes a small `chore: gitignore stray lsl-dummy-stream binary` commit that rode along from the same working session.
- Docs: `docs/how-to/connect-otb-devices.md`, example `examples/otb/muovi_emg.py`, design spec + plan under `docs/superpowers/`.
- **Follow-ups (scoped in the spec):** SyncStation multi-probe path, an in-GUI device-config panel, and Sessantaquattro. A TEST-mode (ramp) first-connect sanity check is recommended on real hardware, but device geometries are now confirmed against manufacturer docs.

body:
Fixes #1725

## Description

This PR resolves the global session invalidation bug where logging out from a single device would forcefully invalidate all active sessions for the user across all devices.

The root cause was that `POST /api/auth/logout` unconditionally incremented the user's `tokenVersion`. This PR fixes it by:
- Adding a `BlacklistedToken` model to the database to track invalidated tokens by their JWT ID (`jti`).
- Automatically attaching a unique `jti` to all custom bearer tokens and NextAuth session cookies.
- Refactoring `POST /api/auth/logout` to only blacklist the current token's `jti` by default, leaving `tokenVersion` intact so other devices remain active.
- Maintaining the old `tokenVersion` increment behavior only for password changes and explicit "logout from all devices" requests.
- Adding a background service (`tokenCleanupService.ts`) to prune expired blacklisted tokens.

*(Note for reviewers: Requires `npx prisma migrate dev` before deploying to create the new `blacklisted_tokens` table).*

## Token-efficiency program — PR3 of 10 (stacked on PR2 #248)

> Base is the PR2 branch; chain is PR1 #246 <- PR2 #248 <- PR3. Retarget to `dev` as predecessors merge.

### What
Stops the `subagent` tool's `list`/`inspect`/`await` from inlining up to 12KB of raw subagent output per agent by default (a second digest channel).

- Adds `verbosity: receipt | preview | full` (default **receipt**). Bounds: receipt <=280 chars, preview <=2000, full <=12000. `full` is rejected for `list` and requires explicit `ids` for every other action.
- All snapshot paths (list/inspect/await/cancel/pause/resume/steer/progress) go through one bounded preview builder; assignment text only at full verbosity.
- Snapshots add an `agent://<id>` output ref **only when the verified `${id}.md.meta.json` sidecar actually exists** (probed once per action across the record session dir + registry dirs) — never advertises a non-resolving ref. Full output is retrieved explicitly via the hash/size-verified resolver from PR1/PR2.
- Updates the bundled subagent prompt doc.

### Verification
- tsgo clean; biome clean
- subagent + tool-discovery suites: 17 pass / 0 fail (receipt-default no-bulk-leak, preview/full bounds, list+full & full-without-ids rejection, output-ref-only-with-real-sidecar)

body:
## Summary

DUPLICATION-reduction review of `implementation/schemas` (rf2-mse54). The slice already went through the senior sweep, so this is pure DRY — two genuine, behaviour-preserving within-slice duplications consolidated.

## What was duplicated

**1. Clearable atom-backed memo cache** (the rf2-17sqc shape, repeated)
- `validator/default-edn-print` and `walker/extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema` each hand-rolled the *identical* structure: a private `(atom {})`, a `find`/`val` lookup-or-compute body, and a `(reset! cache {}) nil` clear fn. The only difference was the key shape (single `schema-value` vs `[schema base-path]`).
- Extracted **`re-frame.schemas.cache/clearable-memo`** — a factory returning `[memoized-fn clear!]`, keyed on the arg vector (so both arities are handled uniformly; a cached `nil`/`false` is still a hit). Both sites derive their public memo fn + clear fn from it.
- The public clear hooks (`clear-edn-print-cache!` / `clear-sensitive-paths-cache!`) keep their **exact names and docstrings** for the `re-frame.schemas` facade re-exports + the test-fixture. Caching behaviour for callers is byte-identical.

**2. `coerce-opts` → `resolve-frame` pair** (5 sites in storage + 1 in digest)
- The four *read* entry points (`app-schema-at` / `app-schema-meta-at` / `app-schemas` / `app-schemas-digest`) used `opts` ONLY to name a frame, repeating the 2-line `(coerce-opts → resolve-frame)` form.
- Added **`storage/coerce->frame-id`** collapsing it. The two `reg-*` entry points keep the two-step form deliberately — they read further keys off the coerced opts (`:rf/defer-elision-populate?`, `entry-opts`) and so need the intermediate map.

## Correctness

No validation/redaction semantics touched. The memo refactor preserves byte-identical cache behaviour; the frame-id helper is a literal inline of the existing two calls. No spec/010 change (no contract change from a dedup).

## Gates
- `npm run test:cljs` — 5486 tests / 19095 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 warnings (cold install + compile).
- schemas JVM suite (`clojure -M:test`) — 227 tests / 18367 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors (incl. the concurrency-stress harness that exercises the clear hooks).

author: stdiodh
body:
## Title

Type: test: improve coverage and query evidence

## Description

### What

- 콘솔 미션 API 확장 근거를 docs 구조로 분리했습니다.
- JaCoCo 리포트 생성을 추가하고 controller/advice 테스트를 보강했습니다.
- WebFlux DTO validation 실패가 500으로 처리되던 문제를 공통 오류 응답으로 보완했습니다.
- 로또 결과 조회의 purchaseId 조건에 MongoDB 인덱스를 적용하고 executionStats 근거를 문서화했습니다.

### Why

- README 수정 금지 정책을 지키면서 포트폴리오 검토용 근거를 docs에 집중하기 위해서입니다.
- coverage와 query tuning 수치를 실제 명령과 리포트 기준으로 남기기 위해서입니다.
- 검증되지 않은 API latency, throughput, 운영 성능 개선률은 문서에서 배제하기 위해서입니다.

Closes #

## Key Code (Before & After)

### Before
* WebFlux DTO validation 실패가 generic exception handler로 흘러 500 응답이 될 수 있었습니다.

```java
@ExceptionHandler(MethodArgumentNotValidException.class)
public ResponseEntity<ErrorResponse> handleValidationExceptions(MethodArgumentNotValidException ex) {
    // validation response
}
```

### After
* WebFlux validation 예외도 같은 validation 응답 생성 경로를 사용합니다.

```java
@ExceptionHandler(WebExchangeBindException.class)
public ResponseEntity<ErrorResponse> handleWebExchangeBindException(WebExchangeBindException ex) {
    return createValidationErrorResponse(ex.getBindingResult());
}
```

* 로또 purchaseId 조회는 non-unique index를 사용하도록 metadata를 추가했습니다.

```java
@Indexed(name = "purchaseId_1")
private final String purchaseId;
```

## Reason for Change

* controller/advice 테스트가 부족해 API 오류 응답 정책의 실제 동작 근거가 약했습니다.
* coverage 리포트 생성 설정이 없어 coverage 수치를 확인할 수 없었습니다.
* 로또 결과 조회는 purchaseId 조건 조회가 핵심 경로이므로 collection 증가 시 full scan 위험이 있었습니다.
* 합성 10만 건 기준 executionStats에서 COLLSCAN이 IXSCAN으로 바뀌는 것을 확인한 뒤 인덱스를 적용했습니다.

## To Reviewer

* README는 수정하지 않았고, 링크 후보는 docs/readme-link-snippets.md에만 두었습니다.
* coverage gate는 추가하지 않았습니다. 리포트 생성과 측정 문서화만 반영했습니다.
* API latency, p95, throughput은 측정하지 않았으므로 개선 수치로 쓰지 않았습니다.
* 인덱스 추가는 읽기 성능과 함께 쓰기 비용 및 저장 공간 증가 가능성을 docs/query-tuning.md에 기록했습니다.

## Verification

```text
./gradlew clean test jacocoTestReport
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 5s
102 tests completed, 0 failed
line coverage 95.04%, branch coverage 96.34%
```

author: go-to-k
body:
## Summary

`cdkl studio`'s ECS image-pin classification — which decides whether a service
/ ALB-backing-service is a deployed-registry pin and therefore gets an
image-override Dockerfile picker — previously ran **only at boot**. For an
INTRINSIC-ECR image (e.g. `ContainerImage.fromEcrRepository(repo)`) the pin is
only resolvable WITH `--from-cfn-stack`, so setting it in the Session bar after
boot updated the run-time binding but never re-ran the classification — the
pickers never appeared without restarting studio.

Now a Session-bar `--from-cfn-stack` change (`PATCH /api/config`) re-runs the
classification and swaps the served target list under the live socket, so the
image-override pickers appear / disappear under the new binding **without
restarting studio**.

### Changes

- **`studio-server.ts`**: `RunningStudioServer.setTargets(groups, dockerfiles?)`
  swaps the served `/api/targets` JSON atomically (single pre-stringified cell,
  read per request via a getter).
- **`local-studio.ts`**: extracted `classifyStudioTargets()` (annotates a FRESH
  clone of the un-annotated base each call, so a re-classify never inherits
  stale pins) and `reclassifyTargetsOnBindingChange()` (change-gate +
  latest-wins token + fail-soft warn) from the boot classification. The
  `PATCH /api/config` handler re-classifies + swaps **only** when
  `--from-cfn-stack` actually changes (a watch / assume-role toggle does not),
  threading the post-patch binding.
- **`studio-ui.ts`**: `applyConfig` re-fetches `/api/targets` after a successful
  PATCH only when the from-cfn-stack binding changed; running-serve rows are
  preserved across the re-render (driven by `serveState` + `updateServeRow`).
- **`#382` → `#384` rename**: the studio image-override-on-ALB feature
  referenced `#382` (an unrelated merged cloudfront PR) in source comments /
  tests / docs; corrected to the dedicated tracking issue #384.

## Behavior change (additive — no host migration)

cdkd embeds `createLocalStudioCommand` and inherits the re-classify
automatically. `RunningStudioServer.setTargets` is a new additive method on the
handle already re-exported from `src/internal.ts`; a host building a custom
studio server can call it but is not required to.

## Test plan

- **Unit**: `classifyStudioTargets` (pinned flips on `--from-cfn-stack` toggle
  against a fake state, no Dockerfile scan for an all-local app, base groups
  never mutated); `reclassifyTargetsOnBindingChange` (change-gate skips a
  no-op / watch toggle, latest-wins drops a superseded earlier classify,
  fail-soft warns + keeps the prior list, threads the post-patch binding);
  `setTargets` re-serve; a jsdom test that `applyConfig` re-fetches
  `/api/targets` only on a binding change.
- **Integration** (`local-studio`): a new section asserts a `--from-cfn-stack`
  PATCH re-runs classification (the studio log banner) + `/api/targets`
  re-serves the full target list under the live socket. Ran clean against the
  real `cdkl studio` binary; 0 Docker orphans.
- 3-axis review (spec / code / test) clean; the test-review gap (the PATCH
  orchestration was inline + untested) was addressed by extracting
  `reclassifyTargetsOnBindingChange` and unit-testing its branches.

Closes #385
